source_review.identity: The frontier dispatcher checks loaded V2 validator and admission module origins and pins current dispatcher, admission core and V2 current_sources before lock creation. I independently compared the source-pins.json hashes of the shared V2 executor, queue validator, ledger, receipt code and admission core with local SHA-256; all matched.
source_review.admission: The BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction inserts canonical plan evidence, unique output ownership, unique producer-consumer edges and pending rows together. Process-death tests at evidence/owner/frontier insertion and postcommit support rollback-before-commit and exact-retained postcommit behavior.
source_review.readiness: The ready_frontier/remaining count is a scheduling projection, not an authorization source: before reservation, binding() re-derives every declared dependency from producer release/result/terminal/output facts and verifies their pins. It also repeats the chain check after executor preparation immediately before launch. A stale undercount therefore fails closed when the producer has no valid release; selected producer-output tampering is covered by the supplied test.
source_review.reservation_and_release: Capacity is structurally one active slot. Reservation/removal from pending is one DB transaction. The external release file is published before the release row/count-decrement/active-slot deletion transaction; a crash in that gap leaves active capacity held and retry verifies/reuses the exact file before committing the DB transition. A crash after commit preserves the downstream ready count. Supplied real process-death tests exercise these boundaries and replay.
source_review.branching: The frontier stores one edge per producer/consumer, even if multiple output roles from that producer are requested. The additional tiny test confirmed both roles bind and two consumers awaken after one producer release. Capacity contention retains a single active attempt. Failed producer directly blocks consumers; grandchildren stay waiting and queue completion is explicitly not inferred from an empty ready frontier.
source_review.measurements: The fixed SQL selection counts are supported for the exact query/schema fixture and grow with unauthenticated synthetic history in the old query, while the new active/ready queries remain fixed across tested sizes. The fixture is in-memory and is not passed to tick or authenticated as execution history. This does not establish full dispatch cost, authenticated-history scale, physical I/O, or thousands-cycle throughput.

material_gaps_and_limits: No concrete false-launch or transaction/replay defect found in frozen code under its declared contract.

The trusted mutable SQLite/cooperating-writer assumption is material: coherent external database/file rewrites, raw concurrent SQLite writers, rollback/restore, or hostile same-UID changes are not authenticated by a protected archive head. The dispatcher intentionally does not audit arbitrary unselected released history every tick.

A stale positive unresolved count can leave an otherwise runnable job stranded; the structural audit can expose such projection corruption, but no automatic repair or liveness recovery exists. This is fail-closed, but not self-healing.
Failed producer descendants can wait indefinitely; no recursive block propagation, cancellation or completion detector exists. The packet discloses this accurately.

Process-death tests use os._exit and SQLite FULL-sync rollback-journal recovery, not kernel crash/power loss, disk-full/fsync uncertainty or storage corruption. Fresh-root bootstrap crash recovery is absent and should be treated as an orphaned failed initialization requiring manual handling.

Only within-plan dependency graphs are supported. No cross-plan dependencies, V2 migration, unattended service lifecycle, large DAG tests, full authenticated historical audit, or production integration is shown.
recommendation: Keep isolated research only. Evidence supports the specific bounded claim that frontier-based selection avoids old released-history SQL scans and that tested local crash/replay transitions preserve readiness/capacity. Before adoption, specify bootstrap/liveness/failed-descendant recovery and durable storage/backup guarantees; then test authenticated large histories and DAGs.
